subject: Priority response + capacity staircase — renewal roadmap
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Howard <lisa.howard@acme.com>, ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2028-08-15T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewals window — capacity & priority response

Hi Evelyn / Ben,

ACME is starting our renewal planning for the platform this quarter. We are seeing consistent growth in inference volume and want to discuss: 1) upgrading our support to a priority SLA, 2) a capacity staircase (20% increase Q4, 40% Q1), and 3) pricing impact for committing to a 24-month term vs 12-month.

High-level asks:
- Concrete latency SLOs for priority customers (tail percentiles for short & long requests)
- Oncall/response commitments (P1/P2 initial response SLAs)
- Estimated uplift in monthly committed spend for reserved capacity to cover 40% ramp

Can we set a call next week? Lisa and procurement will be on the thread for contracting.

Thanks,
Samir
Senior Platform Manager
ACME Corp
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lisa Howard <lisa.howard@acme.com>, ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2028-08-17T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewals window — capacity & priority response

Hi Samir — thanks for the heads up.

We can absolutely support a staged capacity increase and offer a Priority SLA that includes tighter latency SLOs and a 24/7 oncall rota. Ben and I put together a short proposal and ops checklist; Ben will share details below.

Proposed next steps:
- 30-min sync next Tue (Aug 22) to align on volume ramp assumptions
- We’ll run a capacity model and give a committed monthly figure for reserved capacity
- Draft contract addendum with Priority SLA bullets + term options for procurement

Would Tue 10:00am PT work for your team?

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2028-08-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Priority SLA & capacity sketches for ACME renewal (draft)

Samir / Lisa — attaching a concise proposal (see attachment stub: Redwood_Premium_SLA_Roadmap_20280831.pdf) and a preliminary capacity model. High-level items below: 

What Priority SLA includes
- Response: P1 initial response = 1 hour (24/7), P2 = 4 hours (business hours)
- Resolution target windows for common incidents (not a promise to fix code-level bugs immediately)
- Operational credits: scaled credits if monthly availability < 99.5%
- Dedicated triage channel, weekly health check with your ops lead

Latency SLOs (example - measured at ingress for average request size):
- Short requests (<= 128 tokens): 95th percentile < 300 ms
- Standard requests (129 - 1024 tokens): 95th percentile < 700 ms
- Long/streaming (>1024 tokens): 95th percentile < 1500 ms

Capacity staircase (recommended commit levels)
- Baseline (current): X units
- Q4 ramp: +20% committed reserve (lead time: 10 business days to provision burst nodes)
- Q1 ramp: +40% committed reserve (requires reserved pool expansion; estimated 30–45 day lead time)

Pricing sketch
- Priority SLA: +18% on top of committed reserved capacity unit price (volume discounts apply)
- Term incentive: 10% discount on unit price for 24-month commit; 17% for 36-month commit

Action items
- Samir: confirm projected monthly token volume for next 6 months (we used your Q2 figures + 25% growth as placeholder)
- ACME procurement: confirm preferred term (12/24/36)
- Redwood ops (Lauren): validate lead times and run a final capacity test once ACME confirms volumes

Attachments (stubs):
- Redwood_Premium_SLA_Roadmap_20280831.pdf  (proposal & SLO detail)
- ACME_capacity_modeling_20280829.xlsx  (workbook - capacity scenarios)

Thanks — happy to adjust numbers on the sync.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Date: 2028-08-25T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priority SLA & capacity sketches for ACME renewal (ops notes)

Looping in ops detail: a few notes from the engineering/onboarding side before we lock numbers.

- Provisioning cadence: for a +20% burst we can leverage autoscale within 10 business days but to guarantee reserved capacity we need a formal commit and an allocation ticket (30–45 days for sustained pool increases).
- KV/prefix cache warming: to preserve latency SLOs during ramp, we recommend a staged traffic shift (10% increments over 48 hours) and a pre-warm run with synthetic traffic.
- Oncall coverage: Redwood will include a named oncall rotation; we’ll provide contact roster and escalation matrix in the addendum.

Operations asks from ACME:
1) Acceptance window for capacity tests (preferred: 2 business days after provisioning)
2) A primary ops contact (Slack + phone) for incident escalations

I’ll run the capacity scenarios in ACME_capacity_modeling_20280829.xlsx and share results by Fri.

—Lauren
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Date: 2028-08-29T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priority SLA & capacity sketches for ACME renewal (legal/terms)

Quick legal notes to feed into procurement: 
- Term options: 12, 24, 36 months — we recommend using a 24-month term for predictable capacity planning; include early termination clause with 90 days notice + pro-rated termination fee for reserved capacity commitments.
- SLA credits: tie availability credits to measurable platform availability (ingress + model-serving) and cap aggregate credits at 50% of monthly committed fees.
- Data residency & compliance: confirm no additional compliance constraints (ACME mentioned EU customers last quarter) — if EU residency required we’ll need a private deployment addendum and different pricing.

I will prepare an addendum draft to attach to the master services agreement; expect a first redline by Tue.

Rgds,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-09-01T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Final: Priority SLA + capacity staircase proposal and next steps

Hi Samir / Lisa — thanks for the productive discussions. Attached is the consolidated proposal (Redwood_Premium_SLA_Roadmap_20280831.pdf) and the capacity workbook. Highlights and next steps below: 

Summary
- Priority SLA: P1 = 1 hour initial response (24/7); Latency SLOs as proposed by Ben (95p: short <300ms, standard <700ms)
- Capacity staircase: Q4 +20% (provisioned as reserved burst), Q1 +40% (reserved pool expansion)
- Pricing: Priority +18% on reserved unit price; Term discounts: 24-mo = 10% off unit price.
- Contracting: Rishi will provide an addendum redline; we propose DocuSign package for signature.

Immediate asks from ACME
1) Confirm preferred term (12/24/36) — 24 recommended for predictability
2) Confirm exact monthly committed token units for the next 6 months (we used placeholders in the workbook)
3) Confirm acceptance of the lead times (30–45 days for reserved pool expansion)

Once we have those, we’ll: 1) finalize pricing & addendum, 2) create a DocuSign packet (link below), 3) schedule a capacity pre-warm and acceptance test.
